verdicts.gapA: The bottom mini-player is the failure: its title "Sprite Fright - Blender Open Movi…" is hard-truncated mid-word, and the bar sits on top of the fourth feed row so "136 views • 6 days ago" is sliced in half — the persistent chrome eats live content instead of reserving space for it. Second worst, in the same chrome family: the four top tabs (flame / feed / TV / bookmark) are icon-only, so the only thing telling you where you are is a thin underline under an unlabelled glyph — close that (labels + a bar that pads the list rather than covering it) and A becomes the stronger shell.
verdicts.gapB: The "Objectifs programme" header block is the mess: a two-line heading collides with a two-line "+ Explorer les programmes" pill, and directly under it sits grey 12px micro-copy that welds a chart legend to an undo rule — "Barre grise : fourchette ou minimum publié · point : ta cote · Retirer s'annule pendant six secondes". That last clause explains a six-second undo for an action the user has not taken yet, in the smallest, lowest-contrast type on the screen; the slider it is meant to explain (grey dot / green dot, no axis numbers) is unreadable without it. Give the heading a single line, label the slider ends, and move the undo message to the moment of undo.

verdicts.notes: A is the only one of the two that is actually a product screen: clear hierarchy (title, then the plain-language explanation of why cote-R bursaries are missing, then what is available now), every amount paired with its funder and a "Vérifié le" date, and full-width tap targets. B is a store/marketing frame — tilted device, clipped sentences, headline dropped over body copy — and fails the stated criterion outright since nothing on it is an empty, loading, or error state. A's weakness is a mismatched CTA and one under-height source chip; B's weaknesses are structural, so the pick is not close.

verdicts.notes: B meets its own bar cleanly: the headline "Ton estimation de ≈ 28,40 dépasse le seuil publié dans 204 programmes de notre base." sits directly on "Vérifié le 25 août 2026", the curve carries "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · bci-qc.ca" plus the honest caveat that it is illustrative and not a statistic of that programme, the estimate is dashed-framed and marked "ESTIMATION ≈ 28,40", and no percentile or admission-chance language appears anywhere. Its real cost is redundancy — the same verification date printed seven times and three cards with identical "Minimum publié 2025 : 22,5 / Préalables couverts" boilerplate — which flattens the list into wallpaper. A is a competent stock Material screen but its centrepiece calendar is misaligned, cramped and low-contrast, and it offers only one weak text action.

verdicts.gapA: The programme list is nine near-identical cards, each repeating the same two lines verbatim — the "SUGGÉRÉ" chip and "Suggéré à cause du mot : santé · profil du DEC" — while the number that drives every verdict, "Ta cote : 31,20 · saisie par toi", is set in the smallest, palest type on the screen directly under the intro paragraph; collapse the repeated boilerplate into one section-level line and promote the cote to a readable, framed value, and the wall of cards becomes scannable instead of nine copies of one card.
verdicts.gapB: The answer card between the question and "OTHER ANSWERS…" prints its own labels upside-down — "cycle lane" is mirrored and "sidepath or protected cycle lane" runs diagonally — and then explains the problem away with "The road in the illustration is rotated the same as its center on the map"; drawing the diagram right-way-up (or letting the user rotate it) would remove the one thing that makes this screen unreadable at arm's length, and would flip my pick.
violationsA: Internal contradiction that reads as an admissibility judgement: the intro says "Aucune évaluation" and the footer says "pas une évaluation d'admissibilité", yet every card renders a verdict on the student — "Au-dessus du minimum · minimum publié 2025 : 22,5" and "En dessous · cotes publiées 2023–2025 : 32,8–33,5" — which is a pass/fail read of the user's own 31,20 against a cutoff.

Dangling separator / inconsistent metadata wrap: the Université Laval cards read "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · uluaval.ca" on one line, while every Université de Montréal card leaves a trailing "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 ·" with the orphaned source chip "admission.umontreal.ca" dropped to the next line.
The circular "+" add controls on each card measure roughly 34pt — below the 44px minimum for a tappable target, and they are the primary action of the list.
violationsB: Unlabelled, unsourced figure: "16577" sits alone beside a star at the top-left with no label, no source and no date.

verdicts.notes: A wins on the visible parts of the brief: a back chevron top-left, one exclusive choice among three large rows with the quiz as the third option, a "SUGGÉRÉ" chip plus a per-card reason on every entry, a footer that says suggestions come from title words, and a plain "Passer cette étape" — suggestions are unmistakably suggestions. Its own worst enemy is honesty, not layout: the screen promises "Aucune évaluation" and then grades the student's cote against every cutoff. B has the stronger single-decision hierarchy and far better touch targets, but an upside-down diagram, a check button parked on top of the answer sheet, and a naked "16577" are craft failures I cannot vote for.

It never shows an estimate, so the confirmed-vs-estimated contrast is asserted rather than demonstrated, and at "3e session" the first-session case is untested. A loses on purpose, not on style — it is a competent chart page attached to a question it refuses to let you answer, with its last chart cut in half by the nav bar.

verdicts.notes: B carries the whole brief per node — programme name, "Minimum publié 2025 : 22,5" / "Cotes publiées 2024-2025 : 30,5-31,0", a status word ("Au-dessus du minimum"), a stamp ("Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · ulaval.ca"), an add affordance and a per-row "× Retirer" — and its numbers are internally honest (5 dates shown + "Afficher les 11 autres dates" = the "16 dates" and "12 mois 16" counters, and "30 jours 0" is right for a September date against October deadlines). Its real craft weaknesses are the unlabelled slider scale, which makes the dot position decorative, and the very low-contrast grey of the verification lines at arm's length. A is a competent dense grid with generous 96px rows, but it answers none of the criterion and leans entirely on unexplained colour to carry meaning.

verdicts.notes: B satisfies the stated criterion outright: all dates are absolute ("1 novembre 2026") with nothing imminent to warrant relative phrasing, each of the five rows carries "Vérifié le 24 août 2026" plus a named source chip (bci-qc.ca, sram.qc.ca), and the empty windows are labelled with their counts on the chip itself ("7 jours 0", "30 jours 0") so no filter can zero out silently — and the counts reconcile (5 shown + "Afficher les 11 autres dates" = "16 dates" = "Toutes 16"). Its weaknesses are hierarchy and grey-on-white body copy that leans light, not honesty; the confirmed 31,20 is explicitly stamped "saisie par toi le 28 août 2026" and no copy predicts admission or ranks programmes. A is a marketing frame around a mostly empty week grid with a mid-word break and a clipped legend, and its smallest tappable items are a third of the required height.

verdicts.gapA: Every programme card is guillotined at its bottom edge: in the "Doctorat de 1er cycle en médecine (MD)" card and again in the "(DMD)" card, the line "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 ·" and the "ulaval.ca" source chip are sliced mid-glyph by the row boundary — the exact sourcing the product rests on is the part destroyed, and the fixed row height also makes card 2 (two-line title) cram "ULaval / Minimum publié 2025 : 22,5" straight under the title with none of card 1's breathing room. verdicts.notes: A actually does the work — 232+0+5+0 reconciles exactly with the "PROGRAMMES TROUVÉS 237" header, "31,20" is marked "saisie par toi", each cutoff carries "Minimum publié 2025 : 22,5" with an issuer and a check date, and no copy recommends or predicts — which is why it edges ahead despite failing two of its own three conditions (chips are ragged, and the clipped card bottoms are exactly the artefact of fixed-height virtualisation). B is the more finished screen and has no build-level breakage, but its information design is inert and its own overlay degrades the last row and its own label. This is close: one released row height on A would turn a 2 into a 4, while nothing B can fix would make it the more useful screen.

verdicts.gapA: The "Historique des seuils" card carries one stamp for two figures: rows "2024 · Bas de fourchette 22,0" and "2025 · Bas de fourchette 22,5" sit four lines above a single "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · ulaval.ca" chip, so neither number has a stamp adjacent to it — a reader scanning the right-hand column sees bare figures. Concretely, every figure on it is unsourced and undated — "415K subscribers" under "Blender Studio", "28K views • 1 week ago" under "Base Meshes - Free Asset Bundle", "53K views • 1 week ago" — and closing that alone would still leave the screen a channel video list, not a programme detail.
violationsA: Header figure "COTE R 31,20" (top bar) sits with no adjacent source, no verification date, and no visible marker that it is the student's own entry; the clarification "Ta cote R est celle que tu as saisie" is in the footer, far below the fold.
In "Historique des seuils", the figures 22,0 and 22,5 are not adjacent to a stamp — one card-level "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · ulaval.ca" chip is separated from them by a rule and a row.

Truncated label: the tab row ends in "CHA" clipped at the right screen edge after "PLAYLISTS".
Bottom row of content is clipped mid-thumbnail with no affordance indicating more, and the "SUBSCRIBED" grey ghost pill reads as disabled rather than tappable.
verdicts.notes: A is plainly the programme detail and B is an unrelated video-channel screen, so this is not a close call. A's craft holds up: title-then-action-then-numbers hierarchy is right, the cutoff card pairs "22,5 Minimum publié 2025" with two source chips, the badge "DEC REQUIS, AUCUN COURS PRÉCIS" phrases a catalogue fact, and the curve is explicitly disclaimed as "Courbe illustrative … pas une statistique de ce programme" so it stops short of predicting chances. Its real weaknesses are the flat-looking primary pill, the cramped two-column prerequisite row where "Diplôme d'études collégiales (DEC) reconnu" wraps to three lines beside a wide badge, and stamps that live at card level rather than beside each number.
